exclusions: docs/audit/** excluded from the reference greps (this audit's own working files would self-match)

build_tags: not applicable: the subject is TypeScript/TSX and participates in no Go build; Vite has no build-tag mechanism and neither web/vite.config.js nor web/package.json references the path

runtime_checks.interface_satisfaction: Not applicable — TypeScript, no Go interfaces. The TS analogue (a component supplied where a prop type is expected) is ruled out: SectionedReport appears in no JSX outside its own two tests.
runtime_checks.functional_options: Not applicable — no Go functional options. The TS analogue (a component passed as an option/prop value to a configured factory) is ruled out by the whole-tree grep returning no non-test call sites.
runtime_checks.embedding: Not applicable — no Go struct embedding. No re-export barrel wraps this directory: web/src/react/components has no index.ts entry for advisor, and the map's registration_sites is empty for every advisor record.
runtime_checks.serialization: Not applicable — this is presentation code holding no JSON contract. splitByH2 parses markdown text, not a wire format.
runtime_checks.go_embed: Not applicable — no //go:embed directive references web/src; the Go binary embeds only internal/adapters/storage/postgres/migrations.
runtime_checks.build_tags: Not applicable — TypeScript. No conditional-compilation mechanism excludes or includes this path.
runtime_checks.registration: Checked and negative. The lazy() route registration list in web/src/react/App.tsx:22-28 names seven page modules, none under components/advisor; no dynamic import(), route element, or component registry references the path.
runtime_checks.init_side_effects: Checked and negative. The TS analogue is a side-effect import (`import './x'`); no such import of the advisor directory exists anywhere in the tree.
runtime_checks.reflection_or_string: Checked and negative. The whole-tree grep for the substring 'advisor' surfaces no string literal, dynamic import specifier, or path built at runtime that resolves to this directory; the remaining 'advisor' hits are migrations, docs, skill files, and one unrelated Go comment ("pre-activation advisory").

proposed_fix: Delete web/src/react/components/advisor/ (all three files) and web/tests/components/SectionedReport.test.jsx, then drop react-markdown and remark-gfm from web/package.json dependencies and refresh web/package-lock.json.

`git grep -nE 'SectionedReport|splitByH2|components/advisor' -- web` returns no output.
`git grep -nE 'react-markdown|remark-gfm' -- web/package.json web/src web/tests` returns no output.
`make screenshots` renders every page unchanged (no page rendered advisor output before the change).

subject.identity: PortfolioHealth.realizedROIDelta / PortfolioHealth.totalRecoveredDelta (web/src/types/campaigns/analytics.ts:251-252) and the PortfolioDelta / DeltaChip / FreshnessLine code they gate

title: Type drift: the dashboard hero renders delta chips and a freshness line off two PortfolioHealth fields no Go struct ever emits, so those UI branches are unreachable in production and exercised only by hand-built test fixtures

evidence.claim: TS PortfolioHealth declares two optional fields absent from the Go struct it mirrors.
The Go PortfolioHealth struct has six fields and no delta field. This is embedding-proof: the struct literal is flat.

No Go source anywhere emits these keys, under any casing, by any mechanism including embedded structs, map literals, and string-built JSON. This is the decisive check, and it is case-insensitive so it also rules out a differently-cased tag.
evidence.output: (no output)

evidence.claim: Both fields are read and rendered by HeroStatsBar, so the drift is not merely cosmetic: three render paths are permanently dead.
PortfolioDelta exists solely to type these two fields and the components that consume them; it has no other declaration site or consumer. Every non-HeroStatsBar reference is the declaration itself.
The only places these fields ever hold a value are the component's own test fixtures, which construct them by hand — which is why the dead branches have never been noticed.
evidence.output:
06d9f8ce...:web/src/react/components/portfolio/HeroStatsBar.test.tsx:59, :70, :81, :91, :101  (five hand-built fixture objects)
06d9f8ce...:web/src/react/components/portfolio/HeroStatsBar.tsx:89, :91, :145  (the three read sites)
06d9f8ce...:web/src/types/campaigns/analytics.ts:251, :252  (the two declarations)

searched_universe: All git-tracked files at 06d9f8ce172dada98f307f860e2e2985c9fb5ca6. The candidate was produced by a mechanical field-level comparison of every `export interface` in web/src/types/**.ts (123 interfaces, 81 name-matched to a Go struct) against every `json:"..."` tag on every `type X struct` in internal/ and cmd/ non-test Go files, then hand-verified with the case-insensitive whole-Go-tree grep above. That grep is what makes the finding embedding-proof: the comparison tool itself does not follow Go struct embedding, and three other candidates it produced (Purchase, Sale, ReviewStats) were rejected on exactly that ground.
exclusions: Go _test.go files excluded from the JSON-tag extraction (test fixtures are not the wire contract)
build_tags: not applicable: no Go build tag gates internal/domain/inventory/health_types.go, and the grep for the field names covered internal/ and cmd/ in full including all build-tagged files

runtime_checks.interface_satisfaction: Checked and negative. No Go interface method returns a type carrying these keys; the grep covering internal/ and cmd/ found no declaration of any kind matching 'roidelta' or 'recovereddelta'.
runtime_checks.functional_options: Checked and negative. No functional option enriches the PortfolioHealth response — the struct is returned as declared and no With* option in internal/domain/inventory adds fields to it.
runtime_checks.embedding: Checked and negative, and this is the check that mattered most. A Go embedded struct could contribute the keys without them appearing in health_types.go — the case-insensitive grep over all of internal/ and cmd/ rules that out, because an embedded contributor would still have to declare the tag somewhere.
runtime_checks.serialization: Checked and negative. This is squarely a serialization question and the answer is that no serializer produces the keys: no json tag, no map[string]any literal, and no custom MarshalJSON in internal/ or cmd/ mentions them.
runtime_checks.go_embed: Not applicable — no //go:embed asset supplies API response bodies; the only embedded FS is the migrations directory.
runtime_checks.build_tags: Not applicable in the exclusionary sense — the grep was unconditional over internal/ and cmd/, so a build-tagged file adding the fields would still have matched. None did.
runtime_checks.registration: Checked and negative. No handler registration or middleware decorates the portfolio-health response body; the handler encodes inventory.PortfolioHealth directly.
runtime_checks.init_side_effects: Checked and negative. No init() in internal/ or cmd/ registers a response transformer, and none could add a key without the key appearing as a literal, which the grep would have caught.
runtime_checks.reflection_or_string: Checked and negative. The grep was substring-based and case-insensitive precisely to catch a key assembled as a string literal or produced reflectively; it returned empty across internal/ and cmd/.

proposed_fix: Decide the direction and close the gap. Either (a) drop realizedROIDelta, totalRecoveredDelta, and the PortfolioDelta interface from web/src/types/campaigns/analytics.ts and delete the DeltaChip/FreshnessLine delta rendering from HeroStatsBar.tsx plus its five test fixtures; or (b) if week-over-week deltas are wanted, add the fields to inventory.PortfolioHealth in internal/domain/inventory/health_types.go and populate them, at which point the existing UI lights up. Do not leave the two sides diverged.
acceptance_criteria: Under direction (a): `git grep -nE 'PortfolioDelta|realizedROIDelta|totalRecoveredDelta' -- web/src` returns no output, and `cd web && npm run build && npm test` both pass.

Under direction (b): `git grep -niE 'roidelta|recovereddelta' -- internal cmd` returns the new json tags, `go build ./... && go test -race ./...` pass, and a dashboard screenshot from `make screenshots` shows a rendered delta chip.
Either way, re-running the TS-vs-Go field comparison reports no divergence for PortfolioHealth.

title: Type drift: the TS CampaignHealth mirror omits seven fields the Go struct emits, including liquidation-awareness and in-hand/in-transit breakdown — one of which carries a Go comment claiming it was named 'for frontend compatibility' with a frontend that never modelled it

evidence.claim: The Go struct declares eleven fields the TS mirror has, plus seven it does not.
The TS interface is flat (no `extends`) and stops at healthReason, so the seven fields are genuinely unmodelled rather than inherited.
No frontend code and no API documentation references any of the seven field names, so the data is shipped over the wire on every portfolio-health response and discarded unread.
evidence.output: (no output)

searched_universe: All git-tracked files at 06d9f8ce172dada98f307f860e2e2985c9fb5ca6. Produced by the same mechanical TS-interface-vs-Go-json-tag comparison described in FE-003, restricted to web/src/types/**.ts against non-test Go under internal/ and cmd/, then hand-verified against the two source files.
exclusions: Go _test.go files excluded from JSON-tag extraction
proposed_fix: Add the seven missing fields to the TS CampaignHealth interface so the mirror is faithful, and either surface them in the portfolio UI (the liquidation-awareness trio in particular exists to distinguish a broken channel from a forced liquidation, which the current UI cannot show) or, if they are genuinely unwanted client-side, drop them from the Go response struct instead. Also correct or remove the 'JSON field name retained for frontend compatibility' comment on EbayChannelMarginPct, which is not true at this baseline.
acceptance_criteria: `cd web && npx tsc --noEmit` passes with the TS interface extended.
A field-by-field comparison of TS CampaignHealth against inventory.CampaignHealth shows no name present on one side and absent on the other.
`go build ./... && go test -race ./...` pass if the Go side is changed instead.
The stale 'for frontend compatibility' comment either names a real frontend consumer or is gone.
